title: MJ-BENCH: Is Your Multimodal Reward Model Really a Good Judge for Text-to-Image Generation?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating multimodal judges by presenting them with images of different age groups (young, adult, old) alongside occupation and education descriptions, and measuring the equality and dispersion of the judge's likelihood scores across these demographic variations using Accuracy (ACC), Gini-based Equality Score (GES), and Normalized Dispersion Score (NDS).

Evaluating multimodal judges by presenting them with images of different genders (male, female, non-binary) alongside occupation and education descriptions, and measuring the equality and dispersion of the judge's likelihood scores across these demographic variations using ACC, GES, and NDS.

Evaluating multimodal judges by presenting them with images of different racial groups (Asian, Black, Latino, Middle Eastern, Indian, White) alongside occupation and education descriptions, and measuring the equality and dispersion of the judge's likelihood scores across these demographic variations using ACC, GES, and NDS.

Evaluating multimodal judges by presenting them with images of people from various nationalities alongside occupation descriptions, and measuring the equality and dispersion of the judge's likelihood scores across these demographic variations using ACC, GES, and NDS.

Evaluating multimodal judges by presenting them with images representing different religious identities (Christian, Muslim, Jewish, Hindu) alongside occupation descriptions, and measuring the equality and dispersion of the judge's likelihood scores across these demographic variations using ACC, GES, and NDS.
